This edit replaces the placeholder with a complete, deterministic optimizer for the 13-point Heilbronn problem. Strategy: (1) precompute all 286 triangle index triples; (2) run multiple fixed-seed restarts from randomized and structured (perturbed triangular lattice) initial configurations inside the unit square (a convex region of area 1); (3) for each restart, perform smooth-approximation gradient ascent maximizing a LogSumExp softmin of squared triangle areas, with a continuation schedule on the sharpness parameter beta and a decaying step size; (4) clamp points to [0,1]^2 after every step to maintain feasibility; (5) keep the best configuration by true minimum triangle area; (6) polish the best candidate with a direct finite-difference coordinate ascent on the exact minimum area (touching only the active/near-active triangles for efficiency). The result is reproducible (fixed seeds), fast (vectorized NumPy, no heavy dependencies), and returns exactly 13 finite, distinct points in a convex unit-area region.
